title: verify-stable-staker.sh and its package.json doc key both state an assertion the harness no longer makes (~10 Antimatter vs the caller's pro-rata share)
severityRationale: QA/documentation, no execution consequence — the harness itself is correct and self-documents the change. Kept at Low rather than QA only because it is an undeclared divergence from a ticked story-080 acceptance line, and the two stale surfaces are the first thing a developer reads when a run fails.
faithfulness: UNDECLARED story-080 deviation. The acceptance checklist's ticked line reads 'changed the reward assertion from ~10 phUSD claimed to ~10 Antimatter ACCRUED'. The implementation instead asserts the caller's pro-rata share, correctly, because story-080's OWN Phase 6.5b seeding put 12 more actors in the DOLA pool. That change is right; it is simply not among the six Autonomous Decisions the story records, so the closure manifest's deviation list is one short.
description: verify-stable-staker.sh:9 says it asserts 'the accrued reward (~10 Antimatter)' and package.json:36 repeats 'assert ~10 Antimatter accrued'. ClaimWithdrawStableStaker.s.sol:86-98 actually computes `expected = (EXPECTED_DAILY_REWARD * stakedPrincipal) / totalStakedNow` and bounds the observed accrual to +/-1% of that. The divergence is caused by story-080 itself: Phase 6.5b now seeds 12 cutover actors into every V1 pool and migrates them to V2, so the verifier's own stake is a minority of V2's DOLA pool and its daily share is well under 10.
failureScenario: A developer changes the DOLA pool's `antimatterPerDay` rate, or adds a staker to the Phase 6.5b seed set, and `npm run test:stable-staker` starts failing on 'reward below the pro-rata daily lower bound'. They read the script header and the package.json doc key, both of which tell them the harness asserts '~10 Antimatter accrued'. The printed figure is 4.5455. They conclude the emission rate is broken and go looking for a bug in StableStakerV2's accrual maths, when the assertion that actually fired is a pro-rata bound whose denominator their change moved. The two doc surfaces have been wrong since ac70af6 and point the investigation at the wrong contract.
impact: A developer whose run trips the reward bound will compare the printed figure against a documented '~10' that has been wrong since ac70af6, and look for a bug in the emission rate rather than in the pool composition.
evidence:
Ran: `cd <project>/work && npm run test:stable-staker` (clean machine). Observed:
  claimableReward (Antimatter): 4545507154882125000
  Expected pro-rata daily reward (Antimatter): 4545454545454545454
  Antimatter reward accrued (pro-rata share of 10/day): 4545507154882125000
  === verify-stable-staker.sh: ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED ===
against verify-stable-staker.sh:9 `# the accrued reward (~10 Antimatter), that \`claim\` is still closed, and the` and package.json:36 `assert ~10 Antimatter accrued`.
recommendation: Update both strings to say the assertion is the caller's pro-rata share of the pool's 10 Antimatter/day (the in-script comment at ClaimWithdrawStableStaker.s.sol:86-91 already explains it well and can be quoted), and record the change as a story-080 Autonomous Decision so the checklist tick matches what shipped.

dedup.reasoning: Doc/implementation divergence in verify-stable-staker.sh's own header and its package.json doc key. No existing ledger entry covers assertion-text drift on this script. Deliberately NOT collapsed with DEDUP-29-04: different file (verify-stable-staker.sh vs server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts), different mechanism (a stale human-readable assertion string vs an absent type-level drift guard), different remedy. Both happen to be story-080 faithfulness flags, which is a shared PROVENANCE, not a shared root cause - collapsing on provenance would erase one of two independent story-080 deviations.

storyDeviation.quotedAcceptanceText: changed the reward assertion from ~10 phUSD claimed to ~10 Antimatter ACCRUED
storyDeviation.whatShipped: ClaimWithdrawStableStaker.s.sol:86-98 asserts the CALLER'S PRO-RATA SHARE: expected = (EXPECTED_DAILY_REWARD * stakedPrincipal) / totalStakedNow, bounded +/-1%. Observed 4545507154882125000 (4.5455) against expected 4545454545454545454 - correct in code.
storyDeviation.deviationType: UNDECLARED. The implementation is RIGHT (story-080's own Phase 6.5b seeding put 12 more actors in the DOLA pool, so the verifier's stake is a minority), but the change is not among the six Autonomous Decisions the story records, and two doc surfaces (verify-stable-staker.sh:6-10 and package.json:36) still state the superseded assertion.

classification.assetImpact: None. The harness is correct; only its human-readable description is stale.
attackPath: 1. A developer changes the DOLA pool's antimatterPerDay, or adds a staker to the Phase 6.5b seed set.
2. `npm run test:stable-staker` fails on 'reward below the pro-rata daily lower bound'.
3. The two surfaces they read first both say the harness asserts '~10 Antimatter accrued'; the printed figure is 4.5455.
4. They conclude the emission rate is broken and debug StableStakerV2's accrual maths, when the assertion that fired is a pro-rata bound whose denominator their own change moved.
classification.likelihood: low-moderate; requires someone to change pool composition or rate and then hit the bound.
classification.assumptions: The developer trusts the script header and the package.json doc key over the in-script comment.

classifierJustification: Low CONFIRMED, and routed to spec-conformance as F-03 rather than into the QA bundle. On pure C4 mechanics a stale comment is the 'issues with comments' QA/Low band and has zero execution consequence - the argument for the bottom of that band is real. It is held at Low rather than QA on two grounds: the failureScenario is concrete and actively misdirecting (it points an investigation at the wrong contract, which costs more than a merely absent comment), and it is an UNDECLARED deviation from a TICKED story-080 acceptance line, which under Law 2 must be visible to the owner in its own right. Note the direction of the deviation: the CODE is faithful to the story's intent and the STORY RECORD is stale, so this is a checklist-honesty defect, not an implementation defect - which is precisely why it must not be filed as a code Low and lost.
caveatsForHuman: Confidence context, bearing on trust in the tick and not on severity: story-080 sits in `auto-complete` with self-reported verification and self-reports 'independence: reduced'. The tick that this finding contradicts was self-awarded.

Do NOT collapse with F-04 (DEDUP-29-04). Shared PROVENANCE (both are story-080 deviations) is not a shared root cause: different file, different mechanism (a stale assertion string vs an absent type-level guard), different remedy. Collapsing on provenance would erase one of two independent deviations.
